issues.description: The template repository's declaration of ray_sphere_intersect in ray_sphere_intersect.h lists only three parameters (origin, dir, center), but the implementation in ray_sphere_intersect.cpp (same template) defines the function with a fourth parameter (radius). The solution repository's header declares the correct four-parameter signature (including radius). This mismatch in the template (header vs. implementation) will cause compilation/signature errors and confusion for students: calls in main.cpp pass four arguments (including radius), but the template header's prototype does not match, so code that includes the header may not compile or will have an inconsistent declaration compared to the definition.

The function ray_sphere_intersect represents the same conceptual operation (ray–sphere intersection) but is declared with different parameter lists across artifacts. In the template repository header the function is declared with three parameters (origin, dir, center) while the template implementation (.cpp) defines it with a fourth parameter (radius). The solution repository declares/defines the function including the radius parameter. This signature mismatch (missing 'radius' in the template header) breaks the conceptual/implementation mapping and can cause student confusion and compilation/link errors when they rely on the header declaration in the template.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the header declaration in the template match the implementation by adding the missing radius parameter. For example, change the template header declaration to: bool ray_sphere_intersect(const float *origin, const float *dir, const float *center, const float radius); Ensure both header and .cpp use the same parameter list (and mirror the solution), so students can map the function concept to its implementation and compile the project without signature mismatch errors.
